Statement 1 is correct: 180 degrees at 4 minutes per degree is 12 hours, whether one goes east (12 hours ahead) or west (12 hours behind). Statement 2 is wrong: a person crossing the International Date Line while travelling eastward goes back a day, so Tuesday becomes Monday, not Wednesday.

value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; salt weathering is physical, not chemical

Salt weathering breaks rock mechanically by this expansion, so it is classed as physical weathering, which makes statement 3 wrong.

value: Mudflow and slump are rapid movements

Stratovolcanoes (composite volcanoes) are tall, steep cones built of alternating layers of viscous felsic lava and ash. Felsic lava is thick and traps large amounts of gas under pressure, so these volcanoes erupt explosively. Both statements are correct.

Potholes form when pebbles and boulders caught in eddies are swirled round and round, grinding and drilling into the stream bed. This mechanical grinding by the load is abrasion (corrasion). Attrition is the wearing down of the load particles themselves, corrosion is chemical solution, and solifluction is a mass movement, not a stream process.

value: Cayman Trench and South Sandwich Trench

Statement 1 is wrong: the seven-day interval is between a spring tide and a neap tide; two neap tides are about two weeks apart. At neap tide the Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other with respect to the Earth (statement 2), and the Moon's stronger pull is diminished by the counteracting pull of the Sun (statement 3).

A raster is a simple grid of cells, and remote sensing images are themselves rasters, so the format is directly compatible with them (statement 1). The size of each cell relative to the number of cells covering an area is what defines the raster's resolution (statement 2). Runner-up: 1 only (A), if the examiner read statement 2's wording as an incomplete definition of resolution.

Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores, the disc-shaped protein structures on the centromere of each chromosome. The centriole organises the spindle but is not part of the chromosome, the telomere is the chromosome tip, and the chromonema is the coiled chromatin thread.

Facilitated diffusion is passive movement down a concentration gradient that needs membrane proteins (carriers or channels) to help the molecule across. Not all passive transport is facilitated (simple diffusion is not), it is not active transport, and water crosses membranes passively by osmosis, so A, B and C are wrong.

The sodium-calcium exchanger moves Na+ into the cell and Ca2+ out of it at the same time, two ions in opposite directions, which is antiport. Symport moves two substances the same way, uniport moves one, and aquaporins are water channels.

value: Allosteric enzyme subunits carry a regulatory site besides the active site
reasoning: Allosteric enzymes do not follow Michaelis-Menten kinetics; their velocity versus substrate curve is sigmoidal, not hyperbolic, and they are multi-subunit proteins, so A, B and C are wrong. D is the intended correct statement: allosteric enzymes have regulatory sites in addition to active sites. It is MED only because in some enzymes (such as aspartate transcarbamoylase) the regulatory sites sit on separate subunits, so 'each subunit' is an overstatement.

A complex tissue is made of more than one type of cell working together. Xylem contains tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres, so it is complex. Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are simple tissues of one cell type each.

Apical meristems at the tips of roots and shoots divide continually and increase the length of the plant (primary growth). Collenchyma, endodermis and cortex are permanent tissues that do not divide to produce growth.

The coronary arteries branch from the base of the aorta and supply oxygenated blood to the heart muscle itself. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs, and the renal and hepatic arteries supply the kidneys and liver.

Mammals have a four-chambered heart with complete separation, so blood passes through the heart twice in each full circuit: complete double circulation. Fishes have single circulation, and amphibians show only incomplete double circulation because their three-chambered heart mixes blood.
Cholesterol is a sterol, a steroid lipid found in animal cell membranes and used to make steroid hormones and bile acids. It is not a carbohydrate, protein or nucleic acid.

Xerophytes are plants adapted to dry habitats such as deserts, for example cacti with thick cuticles and reduced leaves. Mesophytes grow with moderate water, hydrophytes in water, and halophytes in salty soils.

value: Heating gypsum at 373 K gives CaSO4 . 1/2 H2O (plaster of Paris), not CaSO4 . H2O

Lead nitrate decomposes only when heated strongly (to PbO, NO2 and O2), so the reaction absorbs heat: it is endothermic. Calcium oxide reacting with water, composting of vegetable matter and diluting sodium hydroxide all release heat.

Of the options given, the Doppler effect is the one used in medical ultrasound: Doppler sonography measures the frequency shift of ultrasound reflected from moving blood to measure flow. Gauss's law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, which means isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist. Ampere's law relates magnetic field to current, and Newton's and Pascal's laws concern mechanics and fluids.

value: Extent of lagging (hysteresis) of B behind H

A larger area therefore means a greater extent of lagging. Energy loss is not offered as an option; runner-up: extent of demagnetization (B), which relates to coercivity (the width of the loop) rather than its area.

A refrigerator moves heat from a cold interior to the warmer surroundings, which by the second law of thermodynamics (Clausius statement) can happen only when external work is supplied. Planck's and Rayleigh-Jeans laws concern radiation, and the first law only states energy conservation.

A prism splits white light into its colours because each colour refracts by a slightly different amount; this splitting into a spectrum is called dispersion. Refraction is the underlying bending, but the effect of forming a spectrum is dispersion.

value: In long sight, the image of a near object forms behind the retina

Positive charges moving north to south and negative charges moving south to north both amount to conventional current flowing north to south. Parallel currents in the same direction attract, so the beams are pulled towards each other (their opposite charges also attract electrostatically). So B is deflected towards A.

Tensile stress over longitudinal strain is Young's modulus, not bulk modulus, so statement 1 is wrong. Fortran was developed at IBM in the mid-1950s (released 1957). Prolog dates from 1972, C++ from the early 1980s and Java from 1995, so Fortran is the oldest.

Natural language processing, which lets computers understand and generate human language, is a major application area of artificial intelligence. A database management system and an operating system are general system software, and a register is a small storage unit inside the CPU.

A bus is a set of parallel wires that carries data, addresses and control signals between internal components such as the CPU, memory and I/O. A hub and a router are networking devices, and a port is a connection point for external devices.

Cache memory is a small, very fast memory placed between the CPU and main memory to hold frequently used data. It is more expensive per byte than main memory, not less, so statement 2 is wrong and the answer is 1 and 3 only.
In the binary system each unit is 2^10 = 1024 times the one below, so 1 gigabyte = 1024 megabytes (= 1,048,576 kilobytes).

The Ramsar Convention, signed at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971, is the intergovernmental treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands and their resources.

Methane, nitrous oxide and fluorinated gases (HFCs, PFCs, SF6) all trap infrared radiation and are listed greenhouse gases. Sulphur dioxide is an air pollutant that forms sulphate aerosols which reflect sunlight and tend to cool the climate, so it is not counted as a greenhouse gas.
